title: Principal Component Analysis (PCA)
subtitle: 3D Orthogonal Eigenvectors & 2D Subspace Projection
summary: Find orthogonal directions of maximum variance and project 3D data onto a 2D subspace.

evaluationChart.title: Scree Plot (Explained Variance Ratio %)
evaluationChart.description: Shows how much total dataset variance is captured by PC1, PC2, and PC3.

advantages: Eliminates multicollinearity by producing orthogonal principal components.
Compresses high-dimensional data while preserving maximum variance.
Reduces noise and accelerates downstream supervised training.
limitations: Linear projections cannot unfold curved manifolds (unlike t-SNE/UMAP).
Principal components are linear combinations, reducing feature interpretability.
Extremely sensitive to feature scales; standardization is mandatory.

formulas.label: Covariance Eigendecomposition
formulas.description: Eigenvectors v_k define orthogonal axes; eigenvalues lambda_k measure variance.

formulas.label: Explained Variance Ratio
formulas.description: Fraction of total variance retained by component k.

hyperparameters.label: 3D → 2D Projection
hyperparameters.description: Smoothly flattens 3D points onto the PC1–PC2 plane (1 = 2D subspace).

codeTemplates.fromScratch:
import numpy as np

def pca(X, n_components=2):
    X_c = X - X.mean(axis=0)
    cov = np.cov(X_c, rowvar=False)
    eigvals, eigvecs = np.linalg.eigh(cov)
    idx = np.argsort(eigvals)[::-1]
    return X_c @ eigvecs[:, idx[:n_components]]
codeTemplates.scikitLearn:
from sklearn.decomposition import PCA
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
import numpy as np

X = np.random.randn(50, 3)
X_std = StandardScaler().fit_transform(X)
pca = PCA(n_components=2).fit(X_std)
print('Explained variance ratio:', pca.explained_variance_ratio_)
